author: Ian Johnson
name: Hardened Web Application
description: A Hardened web application: an implementation library, a host, and a test project.

host.description: Where the application runs. Affects only the host project.

choices.description: Kestrel, without the ASP.NET Core request pipeline. The default.
ASP.NET Core, when you need its middleware, authentication or hosting diagnostics.
AWS Lambda behind API Gateway, with a harness that runs it locally over HTTP.
Google Cloud Run: Kestrel on PORT in a container, with a Dockerfile and a SIGTERM drain.
Azure Functions: the routes behind one anonymous HTTP trigger, in the isolated worker the Functions host starts. Runs locally with Azure Functions Core Tools.

HardenedVersion.description: The Hardened package version to pin. Defaults to the version this template shipped with.

skipRestore.description: Skip the automatic restore after creation.

choices.description: The C# is the contract. Routes are attributes; the OpenAPI document is generated from them.
An OpenAPI document is the contract. The models, service interface, routes and validation are generated from it.
A Smithy model is the contract. Same generated output as openapi, from a different source. Needs the Smithy CLI.

responseModel.description: How a handler declares more than one kind of response.

choices.description: Handlers return Response<T1..Tn>, a struct any C# compiler can build. The declared set reaches the generated document, so 404 and 409 are described rather than implied. The default.
One return type per handler; other statuses are reached by throwing, and [Throws<T>] is how they reach the document.

Handlers return a C# 15 union. Same declared set as response, plus exhaustiveness in your own code. Needs a compiler that can do C# 15 - the .NET 11 SDK - and reports a build error naming LangVersion below it.
The old name for throws; scaffolds the same project. Goes away at 1.0.

client.description: The generated client. A choice rather than a switch so another generator can be a value later without renaming the option.

choices.description: A Kiota C# client in src/Hardened1.Client, generated during the build from the document the library writes, and a test that drives it through the pipeline. The default.
A Refit interface in src/Hardened1.Client, generated during the build by Refitter from the document the library writes, and a test that drives it through the pipeline.
No client project, no tool manifest, no export of the document.

testFramework.description: The test framework the test project runs on. [HardenedTest] reads the same on either; the runner package and the assertion style are what change.

choices.description: xUnit v3. The default.
NUnit 4.

mocks.description: The library a [Mock] parameter's double comes from: one package and one assembly attribute in the test project. [Mock] itself is the same.

choices.description: NSubstitute. The default.
Moq. A Mock<T> parameter is the mock to configure; [Mock] T is the object it produces.
FakeItEasy.

modifiers.comment: The container is the Cloud Run deployment artifact and nothing else's.
The JSON context too. Its whole body sits behind the same condition, so without the exclusion a spec-first project received it as a zero-byte file - which builds, and reads as debris.
The Host's own tool manifest pins the AWS Lambda Test Tool, which the generated Main starts when the application is run locally. Nothing else starts a tool, so the other hosts do not carry it.

Program.cs is kept on Lambda now: the entry point is written rather than generated, so excluding it leaves the project with no Main at all. The socket smoke test still goes, because it binds a port itself and a Lambda application answers through the test tool's API Gateway emulator instead - which the template's own verification covers over a real socket. The same on Azure Functions: the host is a separate process, and the worker rung's [AzureFunctionsWebTesting] is the in-process step above the pipeline.

The Functions host's configuration and the settings Core Tools reads belong to the one host that has a host; the launch profile goes with them, because F5 on a function app is `func start` rather than the project.
The launch profile exists to open /docs on F5. Without the page there is nothing for it to open, and a profile pointing at a 404 is worse than no profile.

One global.json reaches the output. The union model needs the .NET 11 SDK for the keyword; every other model pins the 8.0 line, because the newest installed SDK is not a safe default - a net8.0 project built by the 11 preview writes a test deps.json missing its own ProjectReference.

Everything a client brings, as one unit: the project, the tool manifest that pins the generator, and the tests that drive it. The export property in the library csproj, the testing package and its assembly attribute in the test project, and the client project's lines in the solution file sit behind the same symbol in their own files. The handler tests have a variant per client and one that drives the pipeline directly, and exactly one reaches the output as TodoTests.cs - here the pipeline one, by the same rename the union global.json uses.
Each generator has its own tool manifest, client project and client tests, and the Refit set reaches the output under the names the Kiota set has - the same rename the union global.json uses.

postActions.description: Restore the packages the template pinned.
